items.stem: A conversational assistant does not recognise a user's request. What is the best design response?

options.text: Offer a clear fallback or rephrase prompt and a route to help
options.rationale: Correct: good fallbacks recover the conversation and reduce frustration.
Repetition frustrates users and rarely resolves the issue.
Silent failure leaves the user stuck.

options.text: Guess an action and perform it anyway
options.rationale: Acting on a misunderstood request risks harm.

items.explanation: Correct: good fallbacks recover the conversation and reduce frustration.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve safety in a conversational AI assistant? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Provide clear escalation to a human for sensitive cases
options.rationale: Correct: escalation protects users when the bot is out of depth.

options.text: Set guardrails for risky or harmful requests
Let the assistant improvise medical or legal advice
Hide from users that they are talking to AI

items.explanation: Correct: escalation protects users when the bot is out of depth.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why define a persona and tone guide for a conversational assistant?

options.text: To keep responses consistent and appropriate across conversations
options.rationale: Correct: a defined persona drives consistent, fitting tone.

options.text: Because tone has no effect on users
options.rationale: Tone strongly affects user trust and experience.

options.text: To make the assistant sound human and hide that it is AI
Only to satisfy the design team
options.rationale: Persona guidance serves the user experience, not just the team.

items.explanation: Correct: a defined persona drives consistent, fitting tone.
